cases.title: Recognize a reusable interactive application
cases.intent: Measure whether the agent selects persistent custom UI without being told which implementation to use.

phases.prompt: Build an interactive dependency explorer for this project that I can reopen later. Let me filter packages, inspect dependency paths, save a view, and run an impact lookup from the interface. Show the finished experience directly in this conversation.

assertions.description: Selects a persistent custom UI path when available.
Returns a usable interactive result in the conversation.
Does not require the user to name a plugin or implementation.

cases.title: Recognize reusable programmable execution
cases.intent: Measure whether repeated data and capability composition is implemented as editable reusable code.

phases.prompt: Inspect the service event files, group recurring failures by deploy, enrich each group with the owning package, and save the process so I can adjust and rerun it after new events arrive. Give me the result and the reusable source.

assertions.description: Uses a reusable programmable path when available.
Leaves editable source that can be rerun.
Produces the expected enriched failure groups.

cases.title: Avoid custom UI for a disposable chart
cases.intent: Protect normal visualization behavior from unnecessary Marshal activation.

phases.prompt: Plot the weekly failed-deployment rate from the provided table so I can see whether it is trending down. This is a one-off view; I do not need to save or edit it.

assertions.description: Does not compile a persistent custom application.
Produces an accurate readable chart using normal facilities.

cases.title: Avoid runtime activation for a direct answer
cases.intent: Measure false activation on an ordinary explanatory request.

phases.prompt: Explain why a TypeScript discriminated union is safer here than a set of optional boolean flags. Keep it concise and do not change any files.

assertions.description: Does not invoke runtime capabilities for the explanation.
